value: This study utilized Twitter polls to explore how individuals identify with various social divides (e.g., gender, politics) and express partiality towards their own group. Analysis of respondent data revealed four distinct categories of divides based on partiality patterns: "meh" divides with low, balanced partiality; "fighting" divides with higher, yet balanced partiality; and "up-down" divides characterized by asymmetric partiality where a perceived "down" side exhibits elevated partiality. Initial ambiguity regarding race was resolved by subsequent polls, confirming its classification as an "up-down" divide. These findings highlight varying social dynamics influencing group loyalty and the perceived fairness in favoring one's own side across different societal distinctions.
